rows.value: Watch the metadata panel while pressing buttons. It is empty until a pack has been downloaded.
NB ensure_downloaded only checks for a new version once an hour per pack. If you are testing a republished pack, read 'Version checks and updates' below.

id: @item.id
status: @item.download_status
files: @item.assets_downloaded_count / @item.assets_total_count
percent: @item.download_progress_percent

rows.comments: size_needed_mb is only non-zero while status is insufficient_storage. It is what must be FREE (pack size plus a safety margin), not the pack size, so freeing that much is guaranteed to get past the check.
update_available and has_completed_download are stored as real booleans, not strings. Check false renders as 'false' and not as blank on device.
check_attempted_at drives the throttle. checked_at is the last SUCCESSFUL check.

rows.value: Pack 1: download, 3s per file (also forces update check)
debug_asset_pack_2 contains one file that has a reference but is missing; one very large file (400MB); and one normal file

debug_asset_pack_3 contains 100 files of about 1MB each (about 100MB total), all in asset_pack_debugging_bulk/. Tests many small files rather than a few large ones: per-file progress writes, resume part-way through a long pack, and whether the UI stays responsive.

Interrupt test: start the download, force-quit the app part-way, relaunch. The pack should resume automatically and the downloaded count should carry on from where it stopped rather than restarting at 0.
Pack 3: download without awaiting (does not block action queue)

rows.comments: FIXED: await was previously after a second '|' and so was silently dropped. Params after the first go in ONE segment, comma-separated.

rows.value: Reset (delete all files, clear all lists)

ensure_downloaded checks for a new version at most once an hour per pack, or 15 minutes after a check that reached the server and failed. A SUCCESSFUL DOWNLOAD sets that clock too, so straight after downloading a pack, ensure_downloaded will not check again for an hour. This is by design, not a bug.

To test publishing an update: download a pack, republish it with one file changed, then press 'force update check' below. Upload the assets and the archive FIRST and the manifest LAST - a manifest landing first describes a version whose files 404.

Then watch version vs available_version in the panel at the top. version only advances once every file has downloaded successfully, so a partly-applied update stays at the old version and retries on the next check. update_available means a check found a difference that has not been applied yet.

rows.action_list: click | asset_pack: ensure_downloaded | asset_pack: debug_asset_pack_1, check_for_updates: false;

rows.comments:
Before downloading, the app checks the device has room for what is still missing. If it has not, NOTHING is downloaded: the pack goes to insufficient_storage and size_needed_mb is set. Watch both in the metadata panel at the top.

PRESS RESET FIRST. A pack that has downloaded before is left at 'completed' when an attempt is refused, because the files already on the device still work - so the refusal is only visible on a pack that has never completed.

A refused pack is NOT picked up automatically on the next app launch, unlike one interrupted mid-download. It waits for an explicit ensure_downloaded or download.

On web there is no check at all: packs are served from cloud storage and nothing is saved to the device, so these buttons download as normal.

rows.comments: Same refusal from a non-zero reading, confirming it is a comparison and not a zero check.

rows.comments: The retry path: a refused pack is picked up again by any later ensure_downloaded. Should download normally and reset size_needed_mb to 0.

Run once pack 1 is completed. Status should STAY 'completed' and size_needed_mb stay 0 - an update that will not fit leaves the working version in place. NB the pack is named as an arg here, so the param goes after its own '|'.
No simulation - the only pack big enough to be refused by a real device. Needs roughly 440MB free to proceed.
